A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, algorithms, mathematical figure, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, theorems, proofs, and mathematical constructions, including in its appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper throughout the main text and appendices. Its additional algorithm and probabilistic analyses are not empirical results.

M1.justification: V2 adds LookBeforeYouLeap (Algorithm 1): collect initial mentor labels, select a consistent local policy, and subsequently query and update the policy when states exceed a distance threshold. V1's DBWRQ bucketing procedure is retained as Algorithm 2, AvoidCatastrophe, with a revised prescribed tuning g(T)=T^c.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks empirically. The added multidimensional setting and state-distribution assumptions concern theoretical coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed algorithms. Related-work discussions do not constitute baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Changes to state sampling, action-space assumptions, and query schedules are mathematical model or algorithm changes.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. V1's removed multidimensional failure construction is a theoretical counterexample.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical estimates. The changed concentration inequalities and probability bounds belong to theoretical proofs.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured performance values, rankings, or empirical result entries. Changes to regret and query bounds are theoretical results assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds locality definitions and the multidimensional Natarajan-dimension guarantee, supported by PAC-learning, concentration, and packing arguments in Appendix B. It replaces the hardness proof to address randomized algorithms, reformulates 1D simplicity in terms of mentor-policy segments, and corrects the query-bound prefactor from 2+range to 4+range. Remark B.1 adds a suboptimal-mentor extension under modified assumptions. V1's Section 5 multidimensional failure derivation is removed.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on a 1D guarantee for simple payoff functions and identifies multidimensional extension as an obstacle. V2 makes a conditional multidimensional guarantee for bounded-Natarajan, local policy classes its primary contribution, retains the adversarial 1D result as secondary, and explicitly strengthens the hardness claim to randomized algorithms.

C2.justification: V2 interprets mentor-policy complexity as the central boundary between possibility and impossibility. Sections 4 and 6 add substantive qualifications about computational policy selection, the unresolved locality assumption, and the tradeoff between multidimensional i.i.d. states and adversarial 1D states. V1's discussion of unknown horizons and the failed doubling trick is dropped.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 adds implementation-oriented guidance identifying policy updates and nearest-neighbor distance as the required operations, and discusses nearest-neighbor policies when supported by the policy class. V2 also documents horizon-only tuning for the retained 1D algorithm. These remain mathematical specifications; no code, hardware, or runtime information is supplied.

R1.justification: V1's Function Complexity discussion emphasizes individual payoff-function complexity in contrast to class-based measures. V2 removes that positioning and builds its primary contribution around Natarajan dimension and PAC learning, adding relevant references. It also adds a substantive comparison with Barman et al.'s geometric-mean bandit objective, explaining its difference from the product objective.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, results overview, and conclusion; places hardness before the positive results; introduces a dedicated limitations section; and reorganizes the appendices. The former main-text proof discussion is absorbed into the revised appendix treatment, and terminology shifts from payoff-function simplicity toward mentor-policy simplicity.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with reformatted equations, references, and algorithm displays. V2 adds a new pseudocode block and reformats the retained bucketing algorithm. Figure 1 retains the same mathematical construction but is resized, relocated, and given an expanded caption.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's central dimensionality limitation through a distinct algorithm and accompanying multidimensional analysis, while retaining the 1D approach. Its explicit locality and computational qualifications also clarify what the guarantees establish. The extension remains conditional on i.i.d. states and locality, and the detailed 2D failure example is lost, but the broader supported theoretical account and clearer applicability boundaries represent a substantial overall gain.
